# Operation, Evaluation, and Responsibility

When we transition from technical foundations to full-system operation, our central challenge shifts from building isolated AI generators to governing complete, closed-loop design workflows. In Part III, we put our 8-layer Lighthouse Prompt Stack to work across real spatial accelerators and memory subsystems, measuring what transfers across design problems and evaluating how automated systems perform against matched practical baselines.

Crucially, as we increase design velocity, we must define where machine execution ends and human responsibility begins. We examine how architects maintain exclusive commitment authority over silicon tapeouts, manage multi-million-dollar non-recurring engineering capital, and navigate the evolving legal, economic, and institutional boundaries of AI-assisted chip design.

::: {.callout-crux}
## Guiding questions for Part III

1. Under what conditions does an architectural candidate or simulator result transfer safely to a new technology context without causing negative transfer?
2. How do we ensure human architects retain exclusive commitment authority over silicon capital and baseline contracts in an era of automated synthesis?
:::
